sentences.text: Shri Yogesh Kumar Gupta - Advocate for the applicant.
Mrs. Ranjana Agnihotri-Dy.G.A. for the State.
Mr. Akshat Tamrakar, learned counsel for the responde  ORDER
This is second bail application filed on behalf of applicant Bastaram Marthe under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

2. The applicant is in custody since 18.4.2024 in connection with Crime No.190 of 2024 registered at P.S.Waraseoni, District-Balaghat for the offence punishable under Sections 376(3) and 506 of IPC and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act, 2012.
3. Prosecution story in brief is that at the alleged date, time and place, applicant took away minor prosecutrix and committed penetrative sexual assault upon minor prosecutrix.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that incident is said to have occurred on 04.09.2024 and FIR has been lodged on the next day.
This delay in lodging the FIR has not been explained.
Further, in MLC, no NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:60954 2 MCRC-47666-2024 injuries have been found on the person of the prosecutrix.
Further, after referring to statement of prosecutrix, especially, para 5,6, 14 and 15, it is urged that prosecutrix itself has stated that no incident took place.
Prosecutrix did not support the case of the prosecution.
It is also urged that scene of incident is a public place.
Applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.

Applicant is in Bastaram Marthe vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148724508/
1 jail since 18.04.2024.

sentences.text: On above grounds, it is urged that applicant be released on bail.
5. Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the application.
6. Looking to the age of the prosecutrix as well as DNA report, no case for grant of bail is made out.
7. Accordingly, this second application for bail is dismissed.
